analysis.title: Calm before the storm, or before the deal? + Energy Daily 06/11/26
key_insights: UBS Specialist Sales (Dominic Ellis) says Brent is on track to finish the week about 15% lower on renewed hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict, and he is worried the market is pricing in de-escalation without evidence of real progress.

Reuters reports Iran sent a nuclear proposal to the US via Qatari mediators. Iran's top security official says there will be no negotiations and no reopening of the Strait of Hormuz until the US executes Iran's seven conditions. The author notes oil markets seemed to ignore this reiteration.

Iran's seven demands: lifting of sanctions, release of frozen funds, an end to the US naval blockade, guarantees against renewed US and Israeli attacks and an end to attacks on Iranian allies, withdrawal of US forces from the region, reparations, and acceptance that Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz (possibly with tolls). The author finds major US concessions hard to imagine and sees a return to military conflict as far more likely than diplomatic progress.

Several brokers argue that demand destruction from high oil prices and refining margins pushed the global oil market into surplus in October. The author says this is not supported by the most recent data he has seen and will wait for a UBS energy macro update.
With EU integrated oil names implying about $70/b oil, the author sees considerable scope for further correction in the oil price before sector valuation becomes challenging.

The desk reports the biggest US selloff since Covid on Thursday: Nasdaq closed -6.36% and S&P -4.36%, with $2.3T of US tech market cap wiped out. AI-led selling broadened into a positioning unwind. SOX fell 12%, Autos & Software -4%, Consumer Discretionary & Retail -3%, Financials -3%. The earlier bid to Value disappeared.

The desk cites concern over a slowdown in AI build-out spreading to the wider economy, with press reports that Microsoft is tightening scrutiny of projects and weighing whether to strike new neocloud deals.

In the risk-off move Treasuries rallied with the curve flattening, gold rose 1% and WTI rose 3%. Asia followed overnight: Nikkei -6%, Kospi -5%, TWSE -3.75%, CSI 300 -1.5%, Hang Seng -1.25%. Eurostoxx futures were down 1% early and NDX futures bounced 1% off the lows.

UBS US strategy flags another possible round of retail selling into the weekend and Risk Control Funds needing to sell $100B on the day. The desk says some of the short leg that rallied on the unwind versus AI could give back gains into the weekend.

UBS expects a slightly better than consensus October jobs report: NFP +65k, private payrolls +70k, unemployment 4.14%. UBS expects the firmer print to be largely technical, driven by seasonal flows rather than improved underlying labour demand.

Political backdrop: Republicans lost heavily in the midterms. Hegseth defended the Iran war and vowed to fight impeachment efforts, which the desk says could support oil. Trump predicted a 'big agreement' involving more than Ukraine.

Q3 results: MOL CCS EBITDA HUF555bn was in line with company-compiled consensus of HUF553bn and 6% above UBSe. Net income HUF252bn was 1% below consensus because of a higher effective tax rate. Orlen EBITDA (LIFO) excl. impairments PLN14.8bn was 3% below consensus and UBSe. Net income PLN5.6bn missed consensus PLN7.3bn on a 40% tax rate and PLN1.8bn impairment, with a large working capital build of PLN4.4bn.

UBS research flags US E&P Q3 beats at COP, EOG and Murphy, and TRP, TRGP and CNQ beats. TRP raised guidance and TRGP raised its 2027 dividend. SM Energy sold off sharply on Uinta takeaway constraints, and Liberty Energy fell more than 20% after the midterms.
China state refiners are expected to cut November diesel exports on tight inventories. Energy Aspects trimmed its forecast by 400,000 tons to 580,000 tons, with upward revisions possible.
Ukrainian strikes hit the Ryazan refinery, the second Russian refinery hit that week, ending a pause and deepening Russian diesel shortages.

Enverus: US upstream M&A value rose to $12.6B in Q3 from $11.5B in Q2, and 2026 deal value is $80.5B so far. October deals included EQT acquiring Range Resources for $13.8B and Crescent Energy buying Devon's Eagle Ford assets for $4.2B.

sector_views.rationale: The author sees scope for further oil price correction before sector valuation becomes challenging, since EU integrated names imply about $70/b. He also thinks a return to military conflict is more likely than a deal.

geopolitical: Iran sent a nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar, to be discussed only after the US meets seven Iranian demands. The US is reviewing it.

Trump declined to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the midterms, and Iran plans wider retaliation if war resumes.

Trump predicted a 'big agreement' involving more than Ukraine and possibly all of Europe.

Zelenskiy appealed for energy infrastructure aid at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil markets price de-escalation after Iran sent a nuclear proposal via Qatar, with Brent down about 15% on the week. The midterm results may have raised US willingness to negotiate.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran says no talks or Hormuz reopening until the US executes seven demands. The UBS author finds major US concessions hard to imagine and sees a return to military conflict as far more likely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The author's bear view would be undermined by evidence of real progress, such as the US agreeing to Iran's conditions and the Strait of Hormuz reopening, which Iran had said could happen within 2 days of an agreement.
